extracted.intended_audience: scholars, editors, and general readers of Project Gutenberg eBooks (editors of historical texts and users/distributors of public-domain eBooks)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, editing, and distributing a historical literary work (Thomas Paine's The Age of Reason) including textual-restoration decisions, annotation practice, and legal/redistribution requirements for Project Gutenberg eBooks. Covers both editorial standards and the Project Gutenberg license obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore original chapter divisions and headings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where evidence of an original division exists, restore the original chapter structure and translate or restore original headings (e.g., the editor restored the original seventeen chapters and translated their headings into English).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare translations and manuscript evidence sentence-by-sentence to recover originally intended divisions; restore headings into the edition when sufficient evidence supports them. Use the earliest reliable source (author's manuscript or first edition) as the basis for reconstruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct obvious misprints and unclear punctuation
rubrics_metrics.description: Make minimal corrections: 'my rule is to correct obvious misprints, and also any punctuation which seems to render the sense less clear.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limit emendations to clear typographical errors or punctuation that obscures meaning. Do not alter text for stylistic preference when the original reading is defensible; corrections should be conservative and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow the first edition closely unless emendation required
rubrics_metrics.description: In editing Part I the editor follows closely the first edition and only departs for obvious misprints or punctuation changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the first printed edition as the copy-text for the work, making only necessary corrections. Record any departures and justify them in notes or an introduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide translations and footnotes for foreign-language clauses
rubrics_metrics.description: Translate and supply as footnotes important clauses and phrases from other-language sources (e.g., translations from the French version where important).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a text or variant survives only in another language, supply an authoritative translation as a footnote and indicate its source and relation to the main text; avoid altering the main text to incorporate translated material without clear attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt standard citation format for scriptural quotations
rubrics_metrics.description: When following Paine’s quotations from the Bible, adopt the 'Plan now generally used' instead of overly extended writing out of book, chapter, and verse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a consistent, modern scheme for biblical references (book/chapter:verse or editorially preferred short form) rather than repeating full book/chapter/verse text inline; apply this consistently across the edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document textual variants and editorial alterations
rubrics_metrics.description: Note and document deviations, interpolations, editorial insertions, and errors introduced in later editions or by other editors/printers (e.g., alterations by Priestley, printers’ errors, editorial footnotes turned into text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an apparatus, footnotes, or editorial commentary cataloguing known variants and alterations across editions and translations; indicate where editorial decisions have changed readings and explain rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use internal and external evidence to date and assess manuscript variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ internal clues (e.g., references to astronomical discoveries) and external documentary evidence to assess the date and provenance of manuscript material and variants (e.g., Paine’s reference to 'six planets' suggests pre-1781 wording).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check internal content against historical facts (discoveries, events, publication notices) and compare versions (manuscript, translations, early printings) to determine chronology of composition and probable original readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and report publication history and provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide thorough publication history: dates, places, publishers, pirated editions, stationers’ entries, and relevant correspondence explaining how editions arose (e.g., pirated London edition, copyright entries, letters describing print runs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear account of the work’s transmission (manuscripts, translations, printings, piracies), together with documentary evidence (letters, stationers’ records) to help readers evaluate textual authority and variant readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include editorial intention and limits of editorial intervention
rubrics_metrics.description: State editorial principles up front (what will be corrected, what will be left as in original) so readers understand the extent and limits of intervention (the editor states his rule to correct obvious misprints and punctuation only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an Editor’s Introduction outlining the editorial policy, the copy-text(s) used, treatment of variants, and any systematic changes (e.g., modernization of spelling or punctuation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain and clearly mark authorial quotations and marginalia
rubrics_metrics.description: When the author quotes other texts or when editorial footnotes/insertions exist, preserve or clearly mark these elements so as not to conflate authorial text with later editorial matter (e.g., note when an editorial footnote was raised into the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish authorial text from editorial interpolations/footnotes and flag instances where previous editors altered the text; provide citations to sources that indicate the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include the full Project Gutenberg License with distributed copies
rubrics_metrics.description: To protect Project Gutenberg's mission, any use or distribution of a Project Gutenberg work must comply with the Full Project Gutenberg License and include it with the file (see 'THE FULL PROJECT GUTENBERG™ LICENSE').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When distributing this eBook, preserve and attach the full Project Gutenberg License text; display the required opening sentence prominently whenever a copy is accessed, displayed, performed, or distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display the required Project Gutenberg opening sentence prominently
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever any copy of a Project Gutenberg work is accessed, displayed, performed, viewed, copied or distributed, the specific sentence in paragraph 1.E.1 must appear prominently (including active links to the full license).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the precise sentence (providing the license URL and rights summary) is immediately visible to end users and included with all distributed copies unless all references to Project Gutenberg are removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not remove or detach the full Project Gutenberg License from distributed files
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not unlink, detach, or remove the full Project Gutenberg License terms from this work or any files containing part of this work or any other work associated with Project Gutenberg (see 1.E.4 and 1.E.5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the full license bundled with the file in all distributions and formats; if you provide alternative formats, include the license in each format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with Project Gutenberg trademark rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Gutenberg is a registered trademark and may only be used on or associated with an electronic work by people who agree to be bound by the terms of the Full Project Gutenberg License.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use the Project Gutenberg trademark in commerce or in association with a distributed copy unless you have agreed to the license terms; for alternate terms of use contact the Foundation as per Section 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you remove all references to Project Gutenberg you may distribute publicly-domain works freely (U.S. law)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an individual Project Gutenberg electronic work is unprotected by U.S. copyright law and you are located in the United States, you may copy and distribute it without complying with full license terms provided all references to Project Gutenberg are removed (paragraph 1.C).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide original 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' on request when distributing alternate formats
rubrics_metrics.description: If you distribute the work in formats other than 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' (or the official format posted on www.gutenberg.org), you must, at no additional cost, provide a copy or a means of obtaining the original Plain Vanilla ASCII or official form (1.E.6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the original ASCII/plain text file with distributions or provide an easy, no-cost method for users to obtain it; alternate formats must include the full Project Gutenberg License.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not charge fees for access unless you meet specific commercial terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access, viewing, displaying, performing, copying or distributing any Project Gutenberg works unless you comply with paragraph 1.E.8 or obtain written permission under 1.E.9.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial distribution requires compliance with 1.E.8 (including paying a 20% royalty of gross profits to the trademark owner and providing specific refund/replacement policies) or written permission from Project Gutenberg for other terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial redistribution: royalty, refund and quality obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If charging for copies or access you must pay a 20% royalty of gross profits to the Project Gutenberg trademark owner, provide refunds for users who reject the license within 30 days, and provide replacement or refund for defective works within 90 days (1.E.8 and 1.F.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain clear accounting for royalties, honor refund requests within specified windows, and provide quality replacement copies for defects as described in the license; comply with all other license terms when operating commercially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check local copyright law when located outside the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: The copyright laws of your country govern what you may do with this work outside the U.S.; if you are outside the United States, check local laws in addition to these license terms (1.D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before downloading, copying, distributing, or creating derivatives outside the U.S., verify the work's copyright status in your jurisdiction and ensure compliance with both local law and any additional terms linked in the work.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributors and users should be aware that works are provided 'AS-IS', review the limited replacement/refund procedures, and note the indemnity obligations when altering or redistributing Project Gutenberg works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide right of replacement or refund for defective electronic works within 90 days
rubrics_metrics.description: If a defect is discovered within 90 days of receipt the recipient may receive a refund or replacement of the work from the distributor (1.F.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain channels for users to report defects within 90 days and offer either replacement copies or refunds as described in the license; document and honor such requests promptly.
